Testimony ofRep. Cheryl Golek introducing
LD 1503, An Act to Create a Green Crab Only Wholesale Dealer License
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Marine Resources

Senator Tepler, Representative Hepler, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Marine
Resources, my name is Cheryl Golek, and I represent House District 99, which includes Harpswell and part of Brunswick. I am here today to present LD 1503, An Act to Create a
Green Crab Only Wholesale Dealer License.

I am confident that everyone on this committee understands the severe damage inflicted on our
coastal environment by green crabs. In Maine, these invasive creatures pose a profound threat, particularly to our soft-shell clam industry, eelgrass beds and salt marshes. They devastate clam populations, obliterate vital habitats and accelerate coastal erosion -- all of which compromise water quality and threaten the overall health of the Gulf of Maine ecosystem.
Having lived in my cove for over 30 years, I have witnessed this destruction firsthand. Once
thriving with mussels, clams, razor clams and oysters, this area has seen a tragic decline in just
three short years. While I am encouraged to see that eelgrass is slowly returning, I can confidently say that I haven't spotted a single mussel in my cove for over 7 years, and the
familiar presence of clam diggers has vanished from our shores.

When I received an email from Chair Hepler regarding the proposal for a green crab wholesale license, I eagerly stepped up to sponsor it. I am grateful to John Painter of Lewiston for his

request to create this legislation.

-

Together, we can take decisive action to combat the green crab invasion that threatens our waters. Green crabs are now prevalent in large numbers, and it's clear that they're here to stay. However, they also represent an underutilized resource that we must hamess. The current green crab fishery in Maine is underdeveloped, relying heavily on individual fishermen who bear the
burden of locating and delivering their catch to buyers. This fragmented approach stifles the indust1y's potential for growth and limits opportunities for those willing to harvest this invasive
species.

District 99: Brunswick (Part), Harpswell

By establishing a green crab-only wholesale dealer license, we can create a viable market for
green crabs, allowing businesses to purchase from multiple fishermen and distribute the product
statewide.
LD 1503 aims to establish a green crab-only wholesale dealer license that will empower license
holders to engage in wholesale trade --buying, selling, processing, shipping or transporting green crabs directly from our harvesters. Under current law, such activities are tied to a wholesale
seafood license with a hefty minimum fee of $192.75. In contrast, the proposed fee for a green
crab-only wholesale dealer license is a mere $50, promoting accessibility for aspiring dealers. Importantly, the bill also incorporates stringent measures to ensure compliance. Individuals
operating without the appropriate permit may face penalties outlined by the Department of Marine Resources, which retains the authority to suspend or revoke licenses when necessary.
Furthermore, the bill includes a necessary sunset provision, set to repeal the legislation on Jan. 1, 2031. In the meantime, the department will conduct a thorough review of the effectiveness of the green crab-only wholesale dealer license and deliver a comprehensive report to the 134th Legislature in 2030, along with recommendations for its future.
LD 1503 represents a pivotal opportunity to confront our green crab invasion effectively while
simultaneously bolstering our economy and supporting our working waterfront. Let us act decisively for the sake of our environment and our communities.
Thank you for your time and consideration of the bill before you. I am happy to answer any questions you may have.
District 99: Brunswick (Part), Harpswell

TESTIMONY OF
Deirdre Gilbert
Department of Marine Resources
The Department of Marine Resources (DMR) is testifying
In Support of
LD 1503 An Act to Create a Green Crab Only Wholesale Dealer License Before the Committee on Marine Resources
Sponsored by Representative Golek Date of Hearing: April 17, 2025
Senator Tepler, Representative Hepler, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Marine
Resources, my name is Deirdre Gilbert, Director of State Marine Policy for DMR and I am testifying on
behalf ofthe Department in support of LD 1503.
Under current law, in order to buy, sell, process, ship, or transport any marine species or their parts in the wholesale trade, a person must hold a wholesale seafood dealer license, the fee for which is
$192.75.
Green crabs are an invasive species which likely first came to Maine in ballast water in the mid-1800's. The green crab population has increased dramatically in recent years, coinciding with an increase in ocean temperatures. Green crabs feed on shellfish resources such as blue mussels and soft-shell
clams, threatening the state's important wild fisheries. Recent anecdotal information indicates green crabs are expanding into subtidal habitats.
Due to their abundance and the damage they are causing, there has been interest in developing viable
commercial markets for green crabs, but it has proved challenging. DMR wants to support any efforts
to develop a fishery that could successfully deplete their abundance. Toward that end, the harvester
license is an extremely low cost license, so that licensing does not present a hurdle to anyone who
might wish to attempt this fishery. Similarly, DMR is open to the idea of creating a low cost ($50)
dealer license for green crabs only as LD 1503 proposes, so that a person who wants to attempt to
develop these markets has a low barrier to entry.
The Department appreciates that this has been advanced with a sunset provision, so that we can track interest over a period of 5 years. If people are successful in developing these markets, we are hopeful
that in time, the existing dealer license will prove sufficient for their needs, and this carve out will no longer be necessary.
Thank you for your consideration and I would be happy to answer any questions you may have.

Dear Representatives Golek, Eaton, Farrin, Hepler, Rielly, Simmons, Strout, Thorne, and Senator Moore,
I wanted to thank you for your support of LD 1503 "An Act to Create a Green Crab Only Wholesale Dealer License".
My name is John Painter, I live in Lewiston but fish out of Owls Head where I grew up. I'm a part time commercial green crab fisherman and own a small business "Maine Green Crabs" and fully support this bill as a way create some economic opportunity, and assist the still very small but growing interest in green crabs as a food source, both live and processed (eg fish sauce, powdered broth, etc) and to take the next steps in growing the market. I currently sell green crabs to individuals, restaurants and for public cooking/education demonstrations such as with Maine Food and Beverage Education Center in Wiscasset [see attached link]
While my commercial harvester license allows me to sell what I catch, I cannot buy from other fishermen and resell. Currently I have to peddle my catch, at times driving 90 minutes, each direction. And if the they buyer only wants say 20lbs, that's $20 at current market rates. It's a money losing proposition for me, but every time I tell a Chef or someone who wants to buy my green crabs "no" because it's not worth it, that potential customer has a negative experience. Negative experiences for potential buyers, in a short period of time leads to lack of interest and willingness to utilize green crabs for what ever purpose they had.
Though still a very small piece of the seafood industry in Maine, there is a heart beat for green crabs.
The catch-22 in trying to grow Maine's green crab market is, the existing Maine seafood dealer license is too expensive for someone like me who only wants to sell green crabs. And for people who already have a seafood dealer license, the market and volume for green crabs is just too small to mess with. The result is a lack of reliability and consistency in Maine for the distribution of green crabs.
1

A green crab only wholesale license, with the same intent and spirit of the green crab only harvester license, is realistic way to address that distribution issue. Furthermore I believe because green crabs have already caused so much damage in Maine's coastal waters, and that damage is expected to increase, that creates a special incentive for the Maine Legislature to support ways to address their threat using creative and reasonable means that help expand a market, getting them out of our waters and thus mitigating their impact. The green crab only wholesale license is a low barrier ($50), economic opportunity focused approach to help bring reliability to the distribution of green crabs to purchasers around the state. I hope when the bill sunsets, green crabs will be profitable enough that seafood dealers will have no problem adding them to the other Maine seafoods they sell. This bill has the potential to bring net positive economic and environmental impact to Maine and help prime the pump for the next leg in developing a viable green crab market in Maine, and beyond. https://www.mainetastingcenter.com/explore-classes/eat-the-invasive-a-collaborativegreen-crab-supper
